## Expert role requirement — established 6 September 2026

Every task or experiment in Linear and Notion must explicitly instruct whoever completes it, whether a person or an AI assistant, to act as an expert in the topic or niche most relevant to completing that task. Start each task description with an **Expert role** instruction that names the specific discipline and specialization. For work spanning several domains, name the primary expertise and the supporting specialties needed. Apply this expertise when planning, implementing, and validating the task. Carry the instruction into every new task and subtask, and preserve it when revising or copying tasks.

## Historical checkpoint — 6 September 2026 (not current-build acceptance)

Stocktake based on the local swingmanipulation checkout, Astra assessment, Docs/REFERENCE_ANALYSIS_AND_NEXT_STEPS.md and Docs/HANDOFF_ARM_REPAIR.md. This triage did not rerun builds, tests or video review.

Verified on disk: strike windup/release/recovery 0.575/0.50/0.675 s; combo windup 0.70 s; no Saved/Config/CombatTuning.json; UnrealEditor.modules selects module 1004. Grip trajectories, acceleration/follow-through, directional contact responses and release drive already exist. Preserve substantial uncommitted source and asset work.

Latest arm assets and camera changes remain unverified together. Earlier numerical passes and rejected clips do not certify the repair. Historical 567 combat checks, 56/56 tour, 18/18 motion review and 3/3 automation must retain their build identities. README/VALIDATION include superseded figures.

## Current animation direction — 7 September 2026

**Preserve accepted feel — latest user clarification, 7 September 2026:** The user likes the weight and feel of Astra Ultra's current swings. Preserve that baseline, attack timing, acceleration character, commitment and responsiveness. The rehaul targets arms that fail to convey the swing and the sword's awkward “sprinkler” appearance across the screen. Use Mordhau Montage VI to author coordinated screen-space sword and especially hilt travel, with the arms/body visibly carrying the weapon. This is not approval of the current visual animation or a request to replace the successful combat feel. Any necessary authoritative path change must retain that feel and be checked for reach/contact-time effects.

**Grip diagnosis:** Actual hand placement may already be correct. Awkward arm pose and poor hand/glove model or texture may make it appear wrong. Compare hand/guard/pommel relationships with timestamped Mordhau frames, then isolate pose, geometry/skinning and material using skeleton, neutral-material and textured views. Preserve correct contacts; change grip offsets only when evidence supports it. Record hidden details and inferred 3D values as uncertain.

Idle hands/hilt should sit closer to the stomach/upper abdomen with relaxed arms and torso clearance. Author deliberate body/hand/full-weapon poses and phase curves; generate and adapt motion procedurally. Advanced physics is eligible for source generation, baking or runtime use when it improves animation or saves authoring/iteration, memory or runtime resources. Validate the relevant benefit against a simpler approach while preserving gameplay authority.

## Delivery order

<issue id="7d2e0185-e850-4c36-876e-ede33b401797" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-5/diagnose-handarm-appearance-against-mordhau-and-establish-stomach">MEL-5</issue>: preserve the liked baseline; diagnose hand/arm appearance against Mordhau, repair supported pose/model/material faults and establish lower idle → <issue id="5f44e832-3784-4b9d-91fb-b956aa1309e3" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-6/rehaul-authored-procedural-horizontal-swings-for-a-controlled-playable">MEL-6</issue>: rehaul horizontal hilt/sword/arm performance at matching clocks, coordinated with <issue id="5c855498-1e0e-4573-8cdb-c9b9bfe54b97" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-15/rehaul-full-body-swing-motion-and-overhead-hand-follow-through">MEL-15</issue> full-body/overhead work → integrate existing contact reactions/audio → evaluate moving exchanges and defender readability → <issue id="19f97e19-be76-421e-aac9-cbcf6d95069b" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-11/package-and-play-review-the-current-versus-revised-longsword-exchange">MEL-11</issue> playable visual acceptance.

Deliver both horizontal origins and one overhead; body hit, miss, parry, riposte and short combo; a moving range-edge fixture; chamber/wall regression coverage; first-person/opponent normal-speed recordings with reference-matched hilt/hand close-ups. Record exact source/config/assets/build identity. Verify retained weight, timing and responsiveness plus improved arm participation and hilt travel; path changes require reach/contact checks.

Broader chamber/wall authoring (<issue id="dec4f759-5386-49de-ae9a-509ad3b901d1" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-12/extend-accepted-exchange-feedback-to-chamber-and-wall-contact">MEL-12</issue>) and remaining overhead/underhand/stab expansion (<issue id="47a3c647-a3ba-4ba6-849e-e6f905b91bd6" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-13/author-distinct-overhead-underhand-and-stab-motion-after-horizontal">MEL-13</issue>) follow core acceptance. Broad art/weapon/team-mode expansion remains later; targeted hand asset repairs are part of the current diagnosis. Dedicated packaged profiling (<issue id="e2ed049f-e52d-4c55-bfed-a5e7704d184f" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-10/profile-packaged-representative-combat-against-the-694-ms-frame-budget">MEL-10</issue>) remains deferred until playable exchange review unless a concrete slowdown disrupts work. A small technique-specific comparison may justify a physics resource-saving claim without reopening broad profiling. Target 144 fps (6.94 ms) remains a future packaged measurement.

Design source: [Notion Animation](<https://app.notion.com/p/3d32e3c3f8f881e08474defe7febb171>). Original Mordhau Montage VI is available locally; this audit inspected existing 2:44–2:45.875 reference samples, not a fresh full-runtime visual comparison.

MEL-5.title: Diagnose hand/arm appearance against Mordhau and establish stomach-level idle
MEL-5.description:
## Expert role

Act as an expert in Unreal Engine character technical art and skeletal deformation, specializing in first-person arm anatomy, skinning, rigging, grip IK, and motion validation. Apply this expertise when planning, implementing, and validating the task against its acceptance criteria.

The resumed previous arm repair has now been validated and documented in Docs/ARM_REPAIR.md: 18/18 rendered scenarios, 72 skinned captures, zero open arm boundary edges, 1,413,852 sanitized presentation checks and 4/4 engine automation tests. Matched horizontal wrist-axis error improved from 105.712 to 38.973 degrees; all-scenario maximum remains 70.025 degrees. Blade discrepancy was 0.000034 cm and maximum arm edge ratio 1.000128. These verify that checkpoint only and do not establish final visual acceptance. Blocky gloves, extreme-pitch clipping and the rear shoulder opening remain documented. Fingers and shared hip-pivot lean implementation resumed on 6 September 2026 from Docs/HANDOFF_HANDS_AND_LEAN.md; the new work requires fresh validation.

Next actions:

* Preserve the dirty checkout; record source/config/asset hashes and module identity. Archive existing motion frames separately.
* Follow Docs/HANDOFF_ARM_REPAIR.md to run a fresh MotionReview and ArmSkinAudit; inspect all 72 surface samples and 18 scenarios in first person and externally.
* Review wrists, shoulder travel, rigid seams, gaps, intersections and near-plane clipping throughout motion and extreme views. Surface ratio <=1.02 and blade alignment are supporting checks only.
* Fix the observed geometry/pose faults; replace problematic mesh/rig regions if repair cannot produce believable poses. Preserve the verified three-slot armor/glove/arm-steel material binding.
* Run asset/state/frame-rate engine automation after final changes. Publish new evidence in a distinct folder and reconcile README/VALIDATION to this exact checkpoint.

Acceptance: fresh full-motion evidence identifies the exact combined build/assets; visual defects are resolved or explicitly recorded as blocking. No old rejected preview is relabeled as accepted. Native gameplay checks rerun if gameplay changes.

## Animation direction audit — 7 September 2026

**Grip diagnosis — latest user clarification, 7 September 2026:** The hands may already contact the sword correctly. The apparent grip defect could come from awkward arm placement combined with poor hand/glove modeling or texture/material. Treat these as competing or combined causes; do not assume grip offsets are wrong. Compare timestamped Mordhau Montage VI frames for hand order, guard/pommel relationships, spacing, palm/thumb orientation, finger wrap and wrist alignment. Separate actual placement from silhouette, deformation and shading using matched posed/skeleton, neutral-material and textured views. Change grip offsets only when reference evidence supports it; preserve correct contacts. The original footage is available at D:/Mordhau Montage VI.mp4. Existing 2:44–2:45.875 samples were inspected during this audit; hidden details and exact 3D offsets still require annotated reference work.

**Firm idle requirement:** Place idle hands/hilt closer to the stomach/upper abdomen with relaxed arms and torso clearance. Author idle-to-load/parry and recovery-to-idle coherently in first-person and external views. This does not require lowering raised attack preparations or defensive poses.

Next action: create a matched reference/current diagnostic sheet before changing transforms. Compare (1) arm pose and wrist axes, (2) glove/palm/finger geometry and skinning, (3) neutral versus final material/texture. Record which cause is supported, repair or replace deficient hand assets as needed, and preserve correct handle contacts. Deliver idle front/side and first-person close-ups plus continuous idle↔attack/parry/recovery recordings. This is a prerequisite for accepting <issue id="5f44e832-3784-4b9d-91fb-b956aa1309e3" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-6/author-right-and-left-horizontal-swings-for-a-controlled-playable-ab">MEL-6</issue>/<issue id="5c855498-1e0e-4573-8cdb-c9b9bfe54b97" href="https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-15/repair-third-person-swing-biomechanics-and-overhead-hand-follow">MEL-15</issue>, not a claim the old repair is accepted.

Acceptance: the grip reads naturally against annotated footage and the lower idle is convincing; identify whether pose, model, texture, actual placement or a combination caused the defect. No completion based only on IK contact error.

Design: [Notion Animation](<https://app.notion.com/p/3d32e3c3f8f881e08474defe7febb171>).

**Grip diagnosis:** Actual hand placement may already be correct. Awkward arm pose and poor hand/glove model or texture may make it appear wrong. Compare hand/guard/pommel relationships with timestamped Mordhau frames, then isolate pose, geometry/skinning and material using skeleton, neutral-material and textured views. Preserve correct contacts; change grip offsets only when evidence supports it. Record hidden details and inferred 3D values as uncertain.

Reference acceptance: annotate comparable Mordhau/current frames and normal-speed clips for hilt translation, blade orientation, hand travel, elbow/shoulder contribution and camera composition. Inspect load, target passage, follow-through and return; isolate camera motion and allow camera/weapon proportion differences. Confirm that revised motion retains the weight and responsiveness already praised by the user.

MEL-8.description:
## Expert role

Act as an expert in competitive first-person movement design and gameplay physics, specializing in melee footwork, momentum, braking, collision-resolved motion, and repeatable playtest experiments. Apply this expertise when planning, implementing, and validating the task against its acceptance criteria.

Release drive and momentum carry already exist (95 cm/s drive, .72 drive end, .60 carry). Current speeds are 360/315/255/560 cm/s. Evaluate before tuning.

Next actions:

* Compare reach-edge step-in, withdrawal against drag, lateral evasion, whiff punishment, sprint-to-attack, recovery reversal and disengagement.
* A/B current drive/carry against disabled variants; record contact time, distance, stopping/reversal response and perceived control.
* Add one moving range-edge fixture to the core deliverable. Include close bodies and a wall/corner in spacing evaluation.

Acceptance: repeatable results and a documented retain/change decision; steering remains immediate and spacing outcomes predictable. Any changes pass movement and contact regressions across supported frame rates. Do not generalize the historical ~17 cm fixture into universal lunge travel.

MEL-15.title: Rehaul full-body swing motion and overhead hand follow-through
MEL-15.description:
## Expert role

Act as an expert in AAA third-person melee combat animation, specializing in two-handed sword biomechanics, full-body posing, and readable attack silhouettes. Apply supporting expertise in anatomical character modeling, skeletal rigging/skinning, and Unreal Engine procedural animation/IK and authoritative melee trajectories when diagnosing, implementing, and validating this task.

## Problem and observed evidence

The user reports forearm-dominated swings, arms pulled awkwardly in front of the character, an impression of short arms, and overheads ending too high. Repair the third-person movement chain so the body visibly generates the sword and an overhead carries the hands and upper body through the cut.

Source: the attached 31.57-second, 1600×900 user capture, **MeleeCombatLab (64-bit Development PCD3D_SM5) 2026-09-06 14-28-51.mp4**, recorded 6 September 2026. Timestamps below are approximate.

| Capture interval | Observation |
| -- | -- |
| 6.0–9.0 s, front view | Large blade direction changes accompany compact hands/elbows around the upper torso. Body motion exists, but does not convincingly communicate the force of the swing. |
| 17.0–17.6 s, side view | The guard is crowded toward the face/chest, with a tightly folded arm silhouette. This reinforces the apparent short reach. |
| 17.75–19.25 s, overhead | Raised preparation leads to a downward blade, but the hands remain high and elbows fold upward/across the torso before returning to guard. The blade tip reaches low; the missing follow-through is chiefly hand/hilt translation and shoulder/body participation. |
| 20.0–21.4 s, repeated overhead | The same high-hilt, folded-elbow finish repeats. This is a movement-pattern defect, not a single unfortunate still. |

Frame review used a 2 fps overview and 8 fps samples of selected sequences, plus timestamped source crops. The capture does not prove anatomical bone lengths or identify the running module. Reproduce at normal speed before changing the implementation.

[Full-length review video](<https://uploads.linear.app/3c47b17f-90a2-43d9-9a4a-b03074726d26/939ded0f-6a8a-4481-8964-490f4fc9add2/e769c804-932b-4b9b-9b55-bb7fb9ff0061?signature=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJwYXRoIjoiLzNjNDdiMTdmLTkwYTItNDNkOS05YTRhLWIwMzA3NDcyNmQyNi85MzlkZWQwZi02YThhLTQ0ODEtODk2NC00OTBmNGZjOWFkZDIvZTc2OWM4MDQtOTMyYi00YjliLTliNTUtYmI3ZmI5ZmYwMDYxIiwiaWF0IjoxNzg4NzY0NzM1LCJleHAiOjE3ODg3NjUwMzV9.o20TeQypSMUwNHCaXu5SQvoMrgayxrjuWBMkNS1Sz3w>) — compressed to 1280×720 to fit Linear's 10 MB attachment limit; source timestamps retained. The original 1600×900 recording remains at `C:/Users/Daniel Pang/Videos/Captures/MeleeCombatLab (64-bit Development PCD3D_SM5)  2026-09-06 14-28-51.mp4`.

![Timestamped overhead crops from the original capture](https://uploads.linear.app/3c47b17f-90a2-43d9-9a4a-b03074726d26/2144651f-6ccf-45eb-9169-1fca366a5b82/250c21cb-5200-4c18-bb9d-f07ee62e42fe?signature=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJwYXRoIjoiLzNjNDdiMTdmLTkwYTItNDNkOS05YTRhLWIwMzA3NDcyNmQyNi8yMTQ0NjUxZi02Y2NmLTQ1ZWItOTE2OS0xZmNhMzY2YTViODIvMjUwYzIxY2ItNTIwMC00YzE4LWJiOWQtZjA3ZWU2MmU0MmZlIiwiaWF0IjoxNzg4NzY0NzM1LCJleHAiOjE3ODg3NjUwMzV9.Fa3lEIIJJG8WoHFKiHfInbQJROIZk27EogYmYdkBNog)

## Diagnosis to verify

**Primary hypothesis:** the weapon/grip path, shoulder anchors and final arm solve are poorly coordinated. The solver satisfies handle contacts while producing compressed upper arms and excessive elbow/forearm compensation. Lengthening the arms alone would not establish a convincing power chain.

Current dirty-checkout evidence identifies these investigation points; it is not proof that this exact source produced the capture:

* `MeleePresentationPose.h:9,19–48,89–104`: nominal upper/forearm lengths are 26.1/21.22 cm; shoulder accommodation and a wrist-led elbow pole can trade wrist alignment against an awkward upper-arm silhouette.
* `AttackTrajectory.h:55–72,240–255`: cuts share a rotated grip arc; the world path repeatedly projects the weapon into a **43 cm** reach envelope for each hand. Log pre/post-projection hilt positions to determine whether this compresses an otherwise useful path.
* `KnightPresentation.cpp:134–136,149–219`: pelvis/spine motion already exists, then arms are reconstructed from separate shoulder/hand targets. Inspect whether final component-space posing preserves the intended shoulder girdle and torso relationship; do not diagnose this as simply “no torso animation.”
* `AttackTrajectory.h:107–129`: recovery continues the blade and settles the hilt before returning toward guard; its initial continuation occupies 22% of recovery (about 149 ms at current defaults). Test whether the hand path remains too high or starts its return before a readable body follow-through.

**Complementary references — 7 September 2026:** Ren guides economical, deliberate motion; Kronk tests whether the same coherent hands/weapon presentation survives creative attack lines, tight spacing and transitions between threats. Economy means avoiding compulsory wasted motion while allowing purposeful player expression. Preserve accepted swing feel; do not bake montage camera routes into base attacks. See <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d42e3c3f8f881d8b2e7d845679e8eb7"/> (KRONK-01 / F1–F7, A1–A5).
**Swings must communicate violence and power through readable, economical coordination.** The body and arms explain the sword: purposeful hand/hilt travel connects load → initiation → strike → follow-through → resolution. Use only as much motion as the action needs; larger torso or hand excursions are not a quality goal.
- **Preserve accepted feel — latest user clarification, 7 September 2026:** The user likes the weight and feel of Astra Ultra's current swings. Preserve that baseline, attack timing, acceleration character, commitment and responsiveness. The rehaul targets arms that fail to convey the swing and the sword's awkward “sprinkler” appearance across the screen. Use Mordhau Montage VI to author coordinated screen-space sword and especially hilt travel, with the arms/body visibly carrying the weapon. This is not approval of the current visual animation or a request to replace the successful combat feel. Any necessary authoritative path change must retain that feel and be checked for reach/contact-time effects.
- **Adopted approach:** rehaul the animations through deliberately authored body, hand and weapon poses/phase curves, expanded procedurally. Give horizontal, overhead, underhand and stab families distinct anatomical solutions. Artistic control and believable choreography take priority over literal physical realism.
- **Physics is a tool:** use advanced simulation when it improves final animation or saves production/runtime resources. Consider offline simulation and baking as well as runtime use; compare the relevant quality/cost benefit against simpler methods. Preserve gameplay authority and responsiveness.
- **Grip diagnosis:** Actual hand placement may already be correct. Awkward arm pose and poor hand/glove model or texture may make it appear wrong. Compare hand/guard/pommel relationships with timestamped Mordhau frames, then isolate pose, geometry/skinning and material using skeleton, neutral-material and textured views. Preserve correct contacts; change grip offsets only when evidence supports it. Record hidden details and inferred 3D values as uncertain.
- **Idle:** Place hands/hilt closer to the stomach/upper abdomen, with relaxed arms and torso clearance. Keep raised attack/parry poses where appropriate and author continuous idle↔attack/parry/recovery transitions.
- Shape clear contrast in preparation, acceleration and consequence within believable joint limits. Preserve position and velocity continuity; avoid wasted movement and preserve the swing weight/feel already praised by the user.
- **Ren reference:** treat most camera, aim, footwork and timing changes as intentional, given the user's assessment of Ren's precision and economy. Separate authored hand/weapon motion from deliberate manipulation before borrowing it; do not bake his camera path into the base attack. Own-body amplitudes and exact input/phase boundaries remain uncertain. See <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d42e3c3f8f88199b54eed401936acac"/> (REN-01 / F1–F6 and timestamped R01–R06).
- Misses carry; body hits resist; parries redirect; walls rebound; combos transfer; ripostes convert defense into offense. Synchronize recipient reaction, sound and effects with resolved contact.
- Compose first-person and opponent poses separately around the same authoritative blade. Preserve target visibility and clear commitment.
- Use a tiered gate: cheap geometry checks first, then matched first-person/opponent renders for every meaningful pose or trajectory change. Review key poses plus normal-speed motion; exact endpoints and IK tests cannot certify anatomy, occlusion, transitions or power.
Implementation: <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d32e3c3f8f881028f05c2a960248ff1"/>. Updated 7 September 2026.
</content>

**Current:** six strike origins plus stab; origins name the starting side. Procedural hand/body curves, phase-transfer tangents, reach projection and grip IK exist. The authored-motion pipeline below is the adopted direction, not completed implementation.
**Reference review — Kronk:** Test coherent hand/hilt motion under adjacent attack selections, legal aim changes and footwork, with useful visibility between actions. Default 240 controls are user-supplied source context; they do not establish that a montage path requires that input scheme, a particular sample count or looser turn limits. The project's 240 Hz simulation rate is unrelated. See <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d42e3c3f8f881d8b2e7d845679e8eb7"/> (F6 and A3–A4). These are review proposals, not completed tests or added production scope.
**Target implementation**
1. Author phase-aligned body poses, full weapon transforms including roll, calibrated grips and outcome transitions against the actual skeleton; bake weapon curves for the simulation.
2. Select stance/handedness separately from attack angle. Latch the action at input and blend nearby compatible motion samples with continuous orientation.
3. Apply movement and capped look input; derive collision and the visible sword from the same weapon transform. Give pelvis, chest and shoulders independently timed motion.
4. Apply view-specific body corrections and final constrained grip IK. Author reachable paths; keep corrective displacement small. Control Rig/FBIK are optional tools.
5. Diagnose apparent grip faults against footage, separating actual contact placement from arm pose, hand modeling and material. Preserve correct contacts. Establish a stomach/upper-abdomen idle hilt before authoring dependent motion. Store complete calibrated hand/weapon transforms, including roll and palm offsets. Preserve raised load/parry poses where appropriate; do not globally lower every action.
6. Advanced physics is permitted for source generation, baking or runtime motion when it improves animation or saves resources. Physical accuracy is not an acceptance requirement. If simulation modifies the blade, evaluate its final transform through the same authoritative collision path; presentation-only physics must not detach the visible weapon from gameplay geometry.
**Directional scope:** target 240 selections from approximately 6–8 authored cut anchors and 1–2 stab variants per grip style; validate the required count. Prove a continuous overhead fan first. If adaptation cannot preserve quality, use 6–8 bespoke directions with spatial manipulation.
**Rules:** combos alternate body side, wind up slower than ordinary attacks and cannot chamber. Define vertical-cut stance transitions explicitly. Feints permit defense before cosmetic return completes; eligible strike↔stab morphs communicate changed commitment.
**Audit blockers:** the user likes the current swing weight/feel but reports arms that fail to convey it and a sword that “sprinklers” across the screen. Rehaul the coordinated hilt/sword/arm paths against Mordhau while preserving accepted timing and weight. The apparent grip fault may be pose/model/texture rather than wrong contacts. Lower the chest-crowded idle. The earlier 7 September source snapshot also showed directional boundaries and sampled neighboring hilt differences/reach corrections of about 13 cm; those historical measurements are not a fresh measurement of the changing checkout. Fix these before expanding input. Test angular boundaries, full weapon orientation, phase velocity, grip/anatomy and camera clearance.

visual.text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3d32e3c3f8f881dabc3be8eff5b29360 as of 2026-09-07T09:05:08.695Z: {"title":"Visual Direction"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"📄"} ## Chosen art direction — 7 September 2026 **Grounded medieval construction with sculpted angular forms, broad painted steel highlights and restrained graphic combat effects.** The original Riot-inspired knight portrait is the approved visual anchor. Preserve human proportions, articulated steel armor, dark cloth/mail separation, muted-blue heraldry, warm limestone, quiet surfaces and clear daylight. This is continuous 3D volume with deliberately simplified material response, not porcelain armor or a strict cel shader. The expanded courtyard study was rejected in favor of the original. Keep the original background's broad shapes, simplicity and fighter separation; do not adopt the expanded study's detail density. The slash action image remains an exploratory candidate, not approved anatomy or motion. Prototype a narrow solid-looking silver slash ribbon and a compact angular parry cue at resolved contact, keeping hands, blade and follow-up visible. Preserve existing event identity and combat timing. **Implementation scope:** one knight asset, one longsword asset, one courtyard section and one playable horizontal exchange, reusing assets for the opponent. Annotate the anchor, audit what can be retained/adjusted/replaced, prove materials and lighting in the actual first-person camera, integrate the character in motion, then play-review visual match, combat quality and technical correctness independently. Preserve working combat and defer dedicated optimization unless a slowdown obstructs testing. Final standardization follows playable approval. Implementation brief and uploaded reference: Chosen Art Direction — Playable Slice Implementation Brief. Implementation tracking: [MEL-16 — Playable art-direction slice](https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-16/implement-the-chosen-art-direction-in-one-playable-knight-longsword). Source: user-approved knight exploration and subsequent background rejection in Codex, 7 September 2026. This decision governs the new slice; the supporting principles and audio direction below remain applicable. ## Supporting visual principles **Bright, crisp, grounded medieval competition.** The established setting is a sunlit low-fantasy tournament in a maintained stone courtyard. The latest direction emphasizes clean silhouettes, strong player/background separation, restrained heraldry, and competitive clarity. High fidelity should strengthen these qualities. \[S1, S3–S6\]
Element Direction Practical review criterion
Architecture Pale limestone/sandstone; arcades, gates, readable roofline and landmarks Architecture frames bodies without hiding lower attacks or movement
Composition Open duel space, broad circulation, simple fountain obstacle Range, escape paths, and collision are understandable during combat
Light Clear sunlight, cool filled shadows, stable exposure Weapons and armor remain legible in sun and shade
Knights Functional medieval proportions; steel, mail, padded cloth, leather Clear shoulders, elbows, hands, legs, and attack origin in motion
Weapon Hero-quality blade, guard, handle and steel response Use Mordhau to check actual grip and sword/hilt travel. Diagnose apparent grip faults through arm pose, hand model/skinning and texture/material; preserve correct contacts. Idle hands/hilt sit closer to the stomach. Arms convey the already-liked swing weight; visible reach agrees with damage geometry.
Identity Muted blue and red heraldry; sparing gold Identity reads without ornamental noise dominating the fighter
Materials Believable roughness, modest wear, useful silhouette/detail Steel avoids chrome; stone avoids noisy or stretched texture scale
Combat effects Brief directional gold parry and cyan chamber cues Contact is readable in sunlight and the next attack remains visible
Audio AAA audio quality: rebuild from the ground up around full, clean blade air with no scraping metal; let the whoosh continue through hits. Create punchy, full slicing/metal-on-metal hits; make headshots still higher-pitched and sharper. Add subtle armor rustling tied to movement and weighty metallic parries with a poppy onset and controlled resonance. Edit and layer recordings to create the required texture. Balance the complete exchange so no single sound dominates or masks another; preserve swing, impact and follow-up clarity above ambience. This is the user's 6 September 2026 direction; the first sample selection was rejected.
Working palette from the style record: warm limestone **#C9B892**, shadow blue-grey **#667785**, heraldic blue **#294A68**, muted red **#813D36**, leather **#3C2B20**, and cool neutral steel. The Citadel pass adds charcoal slate and sparing gold. These are working art values, not immutable color specifications. \[D5, D6\] Avoid muddy grimdark grading, heavy fog, noisy fantasy effects, excessive bloom, busy backgrounds, dense debris or foliage in attack lines, oversized fantasy armor, and ornate animation flourishes that hide commitment. The player should read the fighter before the decoration. \[S6\] The fountain is the original courtyard anchor and a readable movement obstacle; the later presentation mandate permits rebuilding the courtyard if that improves the result. Preserve the purpose—orientation, open footwork, intelligible collision—rather than treating the exact fountain layout as sacred. \[S1, S4\] **Quality target:** premium armored duelists, convincing hands and deformation, powerful readable motion, and an attractive tournament space. Procedural fallback assets, successful imports, and sharper materials alone do not establish AAA quality. Broad art expansion follows a convincing exchange. \[S4–S6\] **Performance priority — user decision, 6 September 2026:** Defer dedicated profiling, benchmarking and optimization until the core longsword exchange is playable and its feel has been reviewed. Current effort and token budget should go toward combat feel, arm quality, motion, feedback and iteration. Revisit sooner only for a concrete slowdown that disrupts playtesting or development. The long-term targets remain Competitive at 144 fps / 1080p (about 6.94 ms/frame) on a modern six-core CPU, 16 GB RAM and RTX 3060/4060 or RX 6600/7600-class GPU; High at 90 fps; Showcase prioritizing appearance. Competitive should retain the art direction with expensive features disabled. Representative packaged frame-time measurement is future work and is not an acceptance gate for the current exchange milestone. Source register Chosen Art Direction — Playable Slice Implementation Brief

<content>
## Expert role
Act as an expert in Unreal Engine art direction and character technical art for competitive first-person melee, specializing in sculpted stylization, material authoring, armor articulation and readable combat VFX. Apply supporting animation/IK, authoritative combat and multiplayer presentation expertise. Preserve working systems and prove changes in play.
Implementation: [MEL-16 — Implement the chosen art direction in one playable knight–longsword courtyard slice](https://linear.app/meleeslasher/issue/MEL-16/implement-the-chosen-art-direction-in-one-playable-knight-longsword).
## Outcome and scope
Build one small playable scene that proves the chosen style before expanding production: one knight asset, one practical longsword asset, one courtyard section and one convincing horizontal combat exchange. Reuse the same knight/sword assets for an opponent; a second unique character is out of scope. Review miss, body hit, parry and riposte outcomes within that exchange.
## Approved visual anchor
The original Riot-inspired portrait, 06-riot-inspired.png, is the chosen reference. Its essential qualities are natural human proportions, functional articulated armor, clean angular planes, broad painted steel reflections over continuous 3D volume, dark cloth/mail separation, restrained muted-blue heraldry, warm limestone and quiet daylight shadows.
The expanded courtyard image, 09-expanded-courtyard-v1.png, was rejected in favor of the original. Do not implement its added background density. The action/slash study is exploratory, not approved anatomy, motion or VFX. Porcelain armor was an alternative exploration and is not this direction.
Exact paving, plant placement, arch position and the portrait pose are incidental. Background simplicity, broad forms and fighter separation are essential.
## Implementation specification and acceptance evidence
- Geometry: human proportions; credible overlapping plates, softened bevels, quiet fittings and mail/padding in gaps. Evidence: front/side/back views plus walk, turn, swing and defense clips showing readable elbows and no visible plate intersections or open shoulder seams.
- Materials: shared Unreal parent materials and parameterized instances for steel, cloth, mail, leather and limestone. Decide which broad tonal patches live in textures versus shader response. Steel remains metal with controlled roughness and broad reflections; no chrome, porcelain coating or dense scratch noise. Evidence: a material parameter sheet and matched sun/shade captures.
- Lighting: warm sun, cool filled shadows, stable exposure, restrained highlights and clear contact shadows. Evidence: helmet, hands and sword edge remain distinguishable in both sun and shade without bloom or cinematic grading.
- Animation: resolve topology/UVs, textures, rigging/skinning and hidden surfaces; integrate immediately. Preserve correct grip contacts, stomach-level idle and accepted attack weight/timing. Use IK only where useful. Evidence: both hands remain on the handle behind the guard, wrists and elbows stay credible, and sword/hilt travel reads at normal speed in first-person and opponent views.
- Camera: use the actual first-person gameplay camera; record current FOV and typical engagement distances from the project audit. The portrait camera is only an art reference. Evidence: unzoomed gameplay captures at recorded settings, plus external motion review.
- Gameplay/VFX: one narrow, solid-looking, tapered silver slash ribbon follows the recent blade path; a compact angular parry accent appears at resolved contact. Keep the existing restrained gold parry identity. No magical aura, giant crescents, obscured hands or apparent reach extension. Effects do not pause the clock or fabricate hits on misses. Evidence: normal-speed hit/miss/parry/riposte clips, effect-on/off comparison and visible-blade versus authoritative-hit checks.
- Multiplayer: audit and document which existing system owns combat results, what can be predicted cosmetically and how clients reconcile presentation. Preserve authoritative damage/contact ownership. Evidence: attacker/defender client captures under controlled latency show consistent outcomes, no duplicate impact effects and no cosmetic trail creating damage. If no network harness exists, explicitly record the gap and add the minimal verification path needed for this exchange; do not claim multiplayer correctness from local play.
## Narrow task sequence
1. Annotate the anchor and freeze the brief. Reference: original portrait. Change: numbered visual callouts covering proportion, silhouette, steel, cloth/mail, palette, light and background separation; distinguish essentials from incidental details. Dependency: none. Evidence: annotated reference and signed-off rule/criterion sheet.
2. Audit the existing project. Reference: this specification and existing exchange baseline. Change: retain/adjust/replace inventory for mesh, rig, materials, scene, camera, animation, collision, events and networking; record exact baseline settings. Dependency: task 1. Evidence: inventory, baseline captures and separate presentation versus simulation change list.
3. Prove materials/light in-engine. Reference: original portrait. Change: representative plate, cloth, sword and one courtyard wall using shared materials and restrained sun/shade setup. Dependency: task 2. Evidence: gameplay-camera comparisons and saved parameter values before detailed asset production.
4. Finish and integrate the knight/sword. Reference: original portrait plus accepted MEL-5/MEL-6/MEL-15 motion. Change: model → topology/UVs → textures → rig/skin → engine integration → motion review, reusing suitable assets.
